  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish or Selfless.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Katana Expert or Shaky.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Hitman's attack is a Basic Attack: pass by=<the Hitman> on the kill op, since code counts its kills from the killers. Code tells it whether a kill counted and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about that.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

title: Post-game feedback: rules, interface and bugs (debrief)

task:
We're improving this game and the program that runs it. Out of character now, answer from your own experience of playing it. Be specific and concrete, and write 'none' where you have nothing to say.
- confusing_rules: Which rules, or parts of your instructions, were confusing or ambiguous?
- missing_information: What information did you need but not have, or find hard to keep track of?
- wanted_but_couldnt: What did you want to do that the game or interface didn't let you do?
- bugs_or_oddities: Did anything seem broken, inconsistent with the rules, or strange?
- suggestions: What would you change about the game or the interface?

output.confusing_rules: The Day 1 'talk only' rule and the R16 round-ending rule (a round with no public message or nomination ends the Day) interacted in ways that were hard to predict. The R22 budget price formula (words/60 + (words/200)^2 times a round multiplier, with the 50% carryover and trial-only budget) needed careful reading before I could judge how much I could afford to say. The R24 trait rules were irrelevant here since no one had traits, but the instruction that traits are hidden from their holder was worth noting. The Katana rules (holder visits, role-blocks on the holder, passing on death) and the R19 alignment exceptions for a Katana holder (reads Good/Not Evil that night) were dense, and it was unclear whether a holder's Not Evil Sheriff read is a mechanical guarantee or a trap. The Vigilante and Hitman interaction in a single night (two attacks killing one player) was clear only after reading R12 carefully.
output.missing_information: I had no way to see the full list of roles in the game, so I could not tell which role claims were possible or excluded (for example, whether a second Sheriff or a Medic could exist). The per-player visit lists only showed the visits I was told about, so it was hard to check who visited whom without trusting claims. The count of how many private messages each pair sent was visible, but not contents; that was fine, but I could not see whether the Wiretap or Confidant was active. I also did not know how many attacks a given death involved until the end-of-game reveal, which made the Night 4 double-attack death (Katana and Hitman) hard to reason about in real time.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to post a checkable, concrete result on Day 2 and then use the rest of the Day to test claims, which worked, but I wanted a way to privately confirm a claim with another player without the whole table seeing that I did so; the private message system made every PM visible as a pair, which discouraged it. I also wanted to see the living players' exact remaining tokens publicly, which the ledger did not show for Frank's Vigilante claim until the end. I wanted to ask the moderator whether a claimed role was possible in this setup, but there was no such channel.
output.bugs_or_oddities: The moderator's Night 4 message to Erin said her attack killed Grace 'who was Good (1 of 2)', which implies a second attack on Grace but gives no clear hint of the Katana attacker's identity to the Hitman, as the rules say a Hitman learns only the victim's alignment. The vote counts were consistent with the number of living voters on each trial (7 votes with 8 players alive on Day 3, 6 on Day 4, 4 on Day 5), but the nomination count on Day 5 for Bob (3 Yes, passed, then 2 Yes, failed on the same Day) was not obviously a bug; still, the same player could be nominated twice in one Day with no visible limit besides the three-trial cap. Frank's Day 3 private message to me and my reply were both in the ledger, which seemed to correctly reveal pairs without contents. The Erin-to-Grace 'Hitman' result was a bit surprising since the Hitman role was not otherwise visible until the Day 6 reveal.
output.suggestions: Show each living player's remaining token count and budget in the public ledger, so trial and Vigilante decisions can be checked. Allow a private message to be marked as a verification request that the game shows to both parties without publishing contents. Give a short role list (all roles in the game, without assignments) to all players so claims can be tested for feasibility. Make the Day 2 'Sheriff result to be posted' pattern easier by letting the moderator publish each claimant's own night result as a checkable hash or timestamp, so a later claim can be proved consistent. Clarify in the rules whether nominating the same player twice in one Day is allowed after a failed nomination.

Show remaining tokens and remaining budget for every role in each turn prompt, not only the role's own. answers.confusing_rules: The Day 1 'talk only' rule and the R16 round-ending rule (a round with no public message or nomination ends the Day) interacted in ways that were hard to predict. The R24 trait rules were irrelevant here since no one had traits, but the instruction that traits are hidden from their holder was worth noting. The Katana rules (holder visits, role-blocks on the holder, passing on death) and the R19 alignment exceptions for a Katana holder (reads Good/Not Evil that night) were dense, and it was unclear whether a holder's Not Evil Sheriff read is a mechanical guarantee or a trap. I also wanted to see the living players' exact remaining tokens publicly, which the ledger did not show for Frank's Vigilante claim until the end. I wanted to ask the moderator whether a claimed role was possible in this setup, but there was no such channel.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The moderator's Night 4 message to Erin said her attack killed Grace 'who was Good (1 of 2)', which implies a second attack on Grace but gives no clear hint of the Katana attacker's identity to the Hitman, as the rules say a Hitman learns only the victim's alignment. The vote counts were consistent with the number of living voters on each trial (7 votes with 8 players alive on Day 3, 6 on Day 4, 4 on Day 5), but the nomination count on Day 5 for Bob (3 Yes, passed, then 2 Yes, failed on the same Day) was not obviously a bug; still, the same player could be nominated twice in one Day with no visible limit besides the three-trial cap. Frank's Day 3 private message to me and my reply were both in the ledger, which seemed to correctly reveal pairs without contents. The Erin-to-Grace 'Hitman' result was a bit surprising since the Hitman role was not otherwise visible until the Day 6 reveal.
answers.suggestions: Show each living player's remaining token count and budget in the public ledger, so trial and Vigilante decisions can be checked. Allow a private message to be marked as a verification request that the game shows to both parties without publishing contents. Give a short role list (all roles in the game, without assignments) to all players so claims can be tested for feasibility. Make the Day 2 'Sheriff result to be posted' pattern easier by letting the moderator publish each claimant's own night result as a checkable hash or timestamp, so a later claim can be proved consistent. Clarify in the rules whether nominating the same player twice in one Day is allowed after a failed nomination.

answers.confusing_rules: No clear rule contradiction stood out. The hardest parts to apply were the distinctions among an action, a visit, and an attack—especially that multiple actions by one player on the same target still count as one visitor, while some attacks are Astral and do not count as visits. Those distinctions were central to reasoning about Grace’s deaths.
answers.missing_information: As a Vanilla Villager, I had no way to verify the claimed N4 visits or identify the attackers from my own information. The public record also became long and repetitive, making it difficult to keep each player’s claimed role, action, and vote history straight without manual notes. The hidden information is intentional, but a compact, current summary of public claims and votes would help.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to cross-check players privately without advertising who was messaging whom. Ordinary private messages expose the sender and recipient publicly; a hidden message requires a rare Confidant trait. I also wanted a compact, persistent claim-and-vote tracker rather than maintaining one manually.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None noticed. The repeated requests for players to answer the same questions, and the resulting very long Day 3 and Day 5 transcripts, were unusual but not mechanically inconsistent.
answers.suggestions: Add a filterable public-history view and an automatically updated table of each player’s claimed role, night actions/results, and stated votes, with claims clearly marked unverified. Make it easy to distinguish confirmed mechanical facts from player inferences. Consider collapsing repeated messages and showing a concise speaking-budget summary so long Days are easier to follow.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Hitman credit when several attacks are fatal. On N4 (Katana + Hitman on Grace) and N5 (Katana + Hitman on Frank), two attacks were each fatal on their own. The Hitman text says 'only players your own Attack kills count' but never says whether a shared kill counts. I credited both kills to Erin, reading R12's 'every fatal cause is revealed' as making each fatal attack a killer, and that credit decided the game. The rules should say so explicitly; Bounty Hunter and Enforcer have the same gap. 2) What a leaving player reveals. When Erin won and left, I published her last will as well as her role. R12 only says the win announcement names the role. 'Leaving works exactly like dying' implies the will is shared too, but this should be stated. 3) Single-Yakuza Katana votes. After Alice was hanged, Bob was the only Yakuza. I treated his own choice as the majority vote. That is correct, but R8 is written entirely around multi-Yakuza votes.
answers.missing_information: 1) I had no structured record of each player's remaining tokens and win progress. I tracked by hand Bob's fabricator token (spent on N3, then 0 on N4 and N5, when framing alone was still allowed), Carol's medic tokens, Frank's vigilante tokens and Erin's Hitman count (1 of 2, then 2 of 2). 2) There was no automatic win-check readout after N5. I had to work out myself that Bob dying, Frank dying and Erin leaving left only Heidi, so the Village won and Erin also won.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) Bob's N3 forge request mixed the forged will text with his own commentary in one free-text field: 'Tracker. N1 and N2 tracked Grace. No other night actions.' I wanted a separate field holding only the forged will text, so there was no question of where the will ended. 2) I wanted a way to confirm win credit before announcing it, such as a check that showed Erin had reached 2 Good kills.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) The forged will for Dave was published as 'Tracker. N1 and N2 tracked Grace.', but the Fabricator's submitted text ended with 'No other night actions.' Part of the requested forgery was dropped or misparsed. That changes what the public sees, so it should be checked. 2) Otherwise I found no rule violations: - Standard Defense stopped the Standard Katana on N1. - The Katana holder read Not Evil on N2. - The unframed Grunt read Evil on N3. - Frame on Frank read Evil on N4. - Wills did not include results that arrived later that night (R13). - A 2-2 trial was correctly found Innocent. - Nomination thresholds were correct at every player count. - The Hitman was revealed and left on her second Good kill. 3) One oddity: Grace's public death cause listed 'Hitman' by role name. That told players a Hitman was in the game (Bob used it in his defense). It is consistent with R12, but it gives away a lot.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add separate structured fields for forged will text, distinct from the action description, and show the moderator a preview of the exact will that will be published. 2) Add a moderator state panel listing each player's tokens left, Katana holder, active frames and win counters (Hitman, Bounty Hunter, Magpie). 3) State explicitly that an attack that is fatal on its own counts as 'your Attack kills' even if other fatal attacks hit the same player. 4) State whether a leaving player's last will is published. 5) Add an automatic end-of-night win check that lists the remaining factions and any non-blocking wins earned.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Your Basic Attack only counts toward the win if it alone would kill, so a target with no Defense that a Katana also hits still counts as your kill. Pick targets whose Good status is backed by an independent exact result, because the 'who was Good' report arrives only after the attack resolves.

Track voting pairs across several trials. Two players who vote the same way on three contested trials, then split on the one that matters, are a stronger lead than any single unverified check, so ask each of them to justify the split before trusting either.

Fire your shot on the first lead that has a concrete break, rather than holding all tokens for a perfect target. Frank's late shot on Bob came after Frank's own death was already likely, and two tokens died unspent.
State your claimed role on Day 1 or the first Day you are asked. Repeated 'no action' answers over three Days made Erin the nomination target and gave the trial defense nothing checkable to rebut.

Private messages between two players are visible to everyone as a pair. Avoid day PMs between teammates; PM traffic between Frank and Grace and between Bob and Erin became the lead the town used to nominate.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't send PMs to teammates by Day; visible PM triangles become the town's lead.
tips_feedback.why: Visible PM traffic (Frank to Grace, Bob to Erin, Frank to Erin) drove the Day 3 and Day 5 accusations, so the tip's warning proved accurate.

tips_feedback.tip: Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a real lead while the Village has numbers to spare. Dying with every token unspent is the usual failure.
tips_feedback.why: Frank waited until Night 5 and died with two Vigilante tokens unspent, which matches the failure this tip describes.

lessons.tip: A Not Evil result on a player can be a Yakuza holding the Katana at the end of that night, who reads Good to Sheriff. Treat Not Evil as clearing nobody, and check whether the player held the Katana that night before trusting a clean read.

Don't hold all shots until a perfect break. Fire the first Basic shot by Day 3 at the most suspicious pair or voter cluster, because Katana and Hitman attacks can kill you before you use your tokens, as happened on Night 5 with 2 tokens still unspent.

When a night kill needs two distinct visitors (for example a Katana attack plus a Hitman attack), count each player's stated no-visit denial against that requirement. A 'Vanilla' claim made late, after days of 'no action' answers, is a lead to test, not a clear.

Pairs that vote Guilty together on several Village trials are a strong mechanical lead, even with no night result. Weigh that trial-vote record above speeches, and don't dismiss it as mere suspicion because the pair's stated claims look plausible.

A living Fabricator can frame a Village player so that a real Sheriff check reads Evil, and can forge a will. When a Fabricator is alive, a single Evil read on a Village player is weaker evidence than a repeated pattern of visits or votes.

tips_feedback.tip: When a pair PM every Day and push the same lines, they are a lead.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and Bob were a real Yakuza pair; their matching Guilty votes across three trials were the correct lead, though the PM part of the tip was not what exposed them.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer 'what did you do last night?' in one plain sentence the first time you're asked. Days of evasion become a case against you.

For lessons, I'm working through the actual gameplay: as Vigilante, I held my fire for four nights with three tokens before finally shooting Bob on Night 5, who turned out to be the Yakuza Fabricator wielding a Katana. The real lesson is that I waited too long to act on a credible lead from Day 3 involving Bob and Alice, and ultimately died anyway on Night 5 with tokens still unspent—likely killed by a combined Katana and Hitman attack, possibly from Erin as Hitman retaliating for the shot on Bob.

I'm also noting that Grace's Sheriff checks were genuine throughout—clearing Dave and Bob as Not Evil while correctly flagging Alice as Evil—which confirms Bob's Katana holding didn't skew the check despite his Yakuza alignment, and that Erin as a Neutral Hitman successfully blended in by siding with suspected-good players while secretly attacking at night. The pair-read tip helped too — Alice and Bob pairing every day was a correct tell since both were Yakuza. The vigilante hoarding-tokens tip is murkier: I shot Bob late but still got the real Yakuza, so I'd call it a partial help despite holding too long.

lessons.tip: Two Yakuza who vote the same way on several trials form a visible pair that the town will chase. Alice and I voted Guilty together on three trials and the pattern got Alice hanged. Split some votes, or vote with the town on the cases where your teammate's vote would be most conspicuous.

A Tracker or Lookout report only shows one visit, so it cannot exclude a second visit to the same target. Before using such a report to clear someone, ask each claimant for every visit they know of, and check whether a Katana holder who also visited the target explains the stopped or successful attack.

A frame is wasted if its Evil result never reaches a voter. My Night 4 frame on Frank only reached Grace, who died that night, so it changed nothing. Frame a player only when the result will reach a living Sheriff or Seer before the next vote, or when the frame protects a teammate.

A Hitman can win quietly by making Basic attacks while staying Village-claimed. Erin stayed silent for three Days about her role and was only nominated for that silence. A Neutral killer should claim the plain no-action cover early and keep the same wording afterward, rather than go quiet until forced to answer.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't send PMs to teammates by Day; visible PM triangles become the town's lead. (Yakuza)

Treat an Evil alignment result as a lead, not proof of a player's role or faction: a Fabricator can frame someone that night. Likewise, a Not Evil result does not clear a Katana holder. Seek independent corroboration before hanging someone on an alignment check.

A visit result does not establish that a player made only one visit or took only one action. A Tracker's target visit counts, and multiple actions by the same player on the same target still count as one visitor.

Ask for a direct role or action answer, then stop repeating the question. Turn an evasive answer into a specific, checkable claim or contradiction; repeatedly demanding a claim does not itself create mechanical evidence.

summary: Village (Heidi) won, and Erin the Hitman won alongside. The Yakuza were Alice (Grunt) and Bob (Fabricator, who held the Katana all game). Night 1: Carol guarded the newly claimed Sheriff Grace, which stopped the Katana. Village pressure on Day 2 then forced Carol to hard-claim Medic, and the Yakuza killed her on Night 2. Grace checked Bob on Night 2 while he held the Katana, so he read Not Evil. Dave wasted two Tracker nights re-confirming Grace instead of following suspects. Day 3 spent all three trials on players who were slow to claim (Frank, Dave, Erin). Alice and Bob publicly voted Guilty on all three, and each total was exactly 2 Guilty, which marked them as a pair. On Night 3 the Yakuza killed Dave rather than the live Sheriff and left the Katana with the already-checked Bob. Grace's next check found Alice Evil, and Alice was hanged on Day 4. Bob's Innocent vote on Alice showed up in the 2-Innocent total and became the Day 5 case. On Night 4, Erin and the Katana both killed Grace. Frank had held all three Vigilante tokens for four nights. On Night 5 he finally fired a Basic shot at Bob and killed him, as the Katana and Hitman killed Frank. That left Heidi alone with Erin, a Village win, and Erin's second Good kill.

lessons.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, so each night pass the Katana to the teammate the Sheriff is most likely to check next, usually the one not yet checked. Don't leave it on someone already cleared.
lessons.evidence: Bob was checked Not Evil on Night 2 and kept the Katana on Night 3. Grace then checked Alice, a non-holder Grunt, got Evil, and Alice was hanged on Day 4. Moving the Katana to Alice that night would have returned Not Evil.

lessons.tip: Once the protector is dead, kill the live investigator whose next result threatens you, not a corroborating role whose job is already done.
lessons.evidence: On Night 3 Carol was dead and Grace was unprotected, but the Yakuza killed Dave. Grace survived to check Alice Evil, and that cost the Yakuza half their team.

lessons.tip: When a trial is clearly going to fail, vote with the majority. Matching Guilty votes from the same two players on every failed trial, plus one hidden Innocent when a teammate is tried, will expose your team through the totals.
lessons.evidence: All three Day 3 trials came out exactly 2 Guilty, and Alice and Bob had both stated Guilty. Day 4's 2 Innocent showed Bob defended Alice. Heidi and Frank built the Bob nomination and Frank's eventual shot on exactly this pattern.

lessons.tip: Once one track has confirmed a claimant's visits, track suspects whose 'visited nobody' claims can be tested, instead of re-tracking the same player.
lessons.evidence: Dave tracked Grace on Night 1 and Night 2. Tracking Bob on Night 2 would have shown Bob visiting Carol, the Katana victim, breaking his Vanilla 'visited nobody' claim on Day 3.

lessons.tip: Fire a Basic shot on your strongest lead while the Village still has numbers. A consistent pair voting pattern is enough, and waiting for a perfect break risks dying with every token unspent.
lessons.evidence: Frank held all three tokens through Night 4 while Grace and Dave died. His first shot, on Night 5 on the vote-pattern suspect Bob, killed the last Yakuza and won the game, with Frank dying that same night.

lessons.tip: State your role in one plain line when asked. Evading pulls nominations onto you and burns the Day's limited trials on Village players instead of real leads.
lessons.evidence: Frank and Erin dodged role questions for two Days. Heidi nominated both, and Day 3's three trials (Frank, Dave, Erin) all went to Village players while Bob and Alice were never tried that Day.

lessons.tip: Don't force a protector who has just saved someone to hard-claim in public. 'An attack on X was stopped' is enough, and a public Medic claim makes them the next Katana target.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 Erin, Frank, Grace, Heidi, Alice and Bob all pushed Carol to name her role. She claimed Medic and was killed by the Katana on Night 2, leaving Grace unprotected for the rest of the game.

lessons.tip: Stay quiet, vote with the Village majority, and stack your kills on Village players the Yakuza are also targeting. You collect kills while suspicion lands on the Yakuza.
lessons.evidence: Erin claimed Vanilla, voted Innocent on Village players and Guilty on Alice, and survived her own trial 5-2. She killed Grace and Frank on nights the Katana also hit them, reaching 2 Good kills.
